pages.title: Plan the mug shop
pages.question: What must our one-mug order do?
pages.brief: This page will specify a shop that starts with three ceramic mugs and accepts an order for one mug only while stock remains. Readers will predict the command, decision, recorded event, and stock query for accepted and sold-out cases. A small behavior table will become the acceptance criteria handed to the agent. The page will also distinguish the illustration's supplied opening stock from the initialization the implemented application must perform.

pages.title: Create the shop feature
pages.question: Where do the shop state and events belong?
pages.brief: This page will continue from the working project produced by setup, inspect the generated Counter files, and give an agent the bounded task of introducing the shop's state and events. An annotated file tree will explain Entity, Event, Core, and Feature without teaching every import. Readers will establish opening stock explicitly and inspect how an accepted order changes it. The proposed shop identifiers will be verified before any runnable source is published.

pages.title: Accept or reject an order
pages.question: When should the shop accept or reject an order?
pages.brief: This page will implement the shop's one-mug decision using the current command shape, entity lookup, and explicit accept or reject result. Readers will follow an available-stock case and a sold-out case through the same function, then connect only accepted orders to recorded events. Short source excerpts beside the two outcomes will explain the syntax needed at that point. Missing shop state will receive its own rejection case, without introducing transport or payment behavior.

pages.title: Query available stock
pages.question: How do I read the remaining stock?
pages.brief: This page will turn the shop's current state into a stock query and show why its answer is separate from the event history. Readers will follow one accepted order from three mugs to two, then verify that a rejected order changes neither history nor stock. A compact history-and-answer figure will accompany the projection code and its declared event inputs. The lesson will explain that the HTTP query may need time to reflect an accepted command.

pages.title: Place an order over HTTP
pages.question: How can I place an order through the running service?
pages.brief: This page will register the shop's command and query through its Feature and compose that Feature into the application's named Event Model. Readers will send one accepted order and one rejected order, then inspect the stock query through the running HTTP service. A focused wiring excerpt and adjacent request-and-response pairs will connect source to observable behavior. The tutorial will use verified shop routes and payloads, with broader HTTP and MCP choices linked to their task guide.

pages.title: Test shop behavior
pages.question: What checks show that the shop behaves as specified?
pages.brief: This page will turn the original shop table into repeatable checks for an accepted order, sold-out rejection, missing shop state, and the resulting stock query. Readers will distinguish a decision test from an event replay check and an HTTP scenario, then inspect one intentional failure and its repair. Expected and observed results will appear together. The agent's evidence must include the actual checks run and account for delayed query updates rather than assuming immediate consistency.

pages.title: Keep one mug in reserve
pages.question: How can I change the stock policy without breaking existing behavior?
pages.brief: This page will ask the agent to change the shop so that one mug remains available for in-person sales. Readers will update the behavior table first, inspect the decision diff, and check the new boundary alongside existing accepted and rejected orders. A before-and-after comparison will show which outcome intentionally changes and which must remain stable. The lesson will finish with reviewed source and check results, then link to the reusable agent workflow guide.

notes: Retain all four existing routes. Add only decide-orders, stock-query and http-orders. Seven flat sequential pages.
All briefs describe future lessons, not runnable implemented shop APIs.
Setup owns neo new and first Counter response. CLI has no feature generator.
Current starter uses FeatureAction, appEventModel and EventModel.run. Stock ReserveStock is internal-only.
Keep one-mug orders throughout; final change reserves one mug for in-person sales.
No NeoHaskell execution. Page plans can ship; finished lessons require a checked version-coherent shop implementation.
